# Load required packages quietly
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dotwhisker)  # for dot-and-whisker plots
  library(sjPlot)      # for visualising model effects
  library(ggplot2)
})

metrics_scores <- metrics_data_validation %>%
  group_by(cpg_grouping, model, organ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Rescale MAE (invert so that lower MAE → higher score)
    mae_score = scales::rescale(-mae),

    # Rescale R² to 0–1, where higher values → higher score
    r2_score = scales::rescale(r_squared_value)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    # Composite continuous performance metric:
    # Higher values represent better-performing clocks
    performance_score = mae_score + r2_score,

    # Convert design factors to categorical variables
    cpg_grouping = factor(cpg_grouping),
    tile_methode = factor(tile_methode),
    model = factor(model),
    organ = factor(organ),
    rsq_threshold = factor(rsq_threshold),
    filter = factor(filter),

    # Scale numeric hyperparameters (important for mixed-model stability)
    epse_scaled = scale(epse)
  )

# -----------------------------
# 1. Dot-and-whisker plot of fixed effects
# Visualises estimated effects of predictors on performance_score.
# Points = coefficient estimates; whiskers = confidence intervals.
# -----------------------------
p <- dwplot(m, dot_args = list(aes(colour = factor(term))), whisker_args = list(aes(colour = factor(term)))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = okabe_ito_palette(23)) +
 guides(colour = "none")+
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  ggtitle("Fixed Effects: Dot-and-Whisker Plot")

p

ggsave(paste0(output_directory,"/Dot_and_whisker_plot_of_fixed_effects.png"),

# fit the linear model
lm_fit <- lm(performance_score ~ fitted*organ, data = metrics_scores)
slope_val <- round(coef(lm_fit))

p <- ggplot(metrics_scores, aes(x = fitted, y = performance_score, colour = organ)) +

##  CpG number influence on clocks 
#### Are there any overlapp between cpgs selected and organs 
```{r 34}

################################################################################
# Analysis of Cpg candidate, selected and identity on epigenetic clock performance
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# This script evaluates how the number of candidate and selected CpG as well as identity most  # strongly influence model performance across thousands of clock configurations. Performance is
# represented as a composite continuous metric integrating prediction accuracy (MAE) and       # variance explained (R²).
#
# The workflow:
#   1. Load required libraries
#   2. Construct interpretable performance metrics
#   3. Fit a mixed model to quantify factor contributions
#   4. Extract best-performing models per organ
#   5. Diagnose multicollinearity and correlation structure
################################################################################
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(dplyr)
  library(purrr)
  library(tibble)
})


################################################################################
# 1. Construct a continuous, comparable outcome for model performance
################################################################################

# The underlying assumption:
#   - Lower MAE indicates a more accurate age prediction
#   - Higher R² indicates better variance explanation
#   - Both metrics must be placed on a common scale
#   - A combined score captures overall model performance




metrics_scores <- metrics_data_validation %>%
  group_by(cpg_grouping, model, organ) %>%
  mutate(
    mae_score = scales::rescale(-mae),
    r2_score  = scales::rescale(r_squared_value)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    performance_score = mae_score + r2_score,
    cpg_grouping = factor(cpg_grouping),
    tile_methode = factor(tile_methode),
    model = factor(model),
    organ = factor(organ),
    rsq_threshold = factor(rsq_threshold),
    filter = factor(filter),
    epse_scaled = scale(epse)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    cpg_data_validation_long %>% 
      dplyr::select(unique_model_id, num_selected_cpg, num_candidate_cpg,selected_cpgs, chr,start,end),
    by = "unique_model_id"
  )

################################################################################
# 2. Extract the best-performing model per organ
################################################################################

# These represent the highest-scoring clocks within each biological organ.
best1 <- metrics_scores %>%
  group_by(organ) %>%
  filter(performance_score == max(performance_score))%>%
  dplyr::slice(1)

################################################################################
# 3. overlappingCPGs in best doels and all models 
################################################################################

# all cpgs which repeatidly are selected for each organ seperatly 
Multi_organ_best_cpg <- tibble::tibble(
  organ = names(best_selected_cpgs_organs),
  selected_cpgs  = best_selected_cpgs_organs
) |>
  tidyr::unnest_longer(selected_cpgs, values_to = "selected_cpgs")

# all cpgs which are expressed in all 4 mdoels accross all 4000 runs 
best_cpg_overlap_all_df <- as.data.frame(best_cpg_overlap_all) %>%
  dplyr::rename(selected_cpgs = best_cpg_overlap_all) %>%
  mutate(organ = "Soma")

# cpgs which are expressed in all single tissue mdoels accross all 4000 runs 
best_cpg_overlap_single_df <- as.data.frame(best_cpg_overlap_single) %>%
  dplyr::rename(selected_cpgs = best_cpg_overlap_single) %>%
  mutate(organ = "Soma")


###############################################################################
# 4. Helper function — parse "chr:start:end" into interval table
###############################################################################

parse_cpg_intervals <- function(cpg_vector) {
  dt <- tstrsplit(cpg_vector, ":", fixed = TRUE)
  data.table(
    chr   = as.integer(dt[[1]]),
    start = as.integer(dt[[2]]),
    end   = as.integer(dt[[3]]),
    cpg_id = cpg_vector
  )
}

###############################################################################
# 5. Build interval lists per organ
###############################################################################

# ---- ALL MODELS ----
cpg_intervals_all <- cpg_data_validation_long %>%
  group_by(organ) %>%
  summarise(cpgs = list(unique(selected_cpgs)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(intervals = map(cpgs, parse_cpg_intervals)) %>%
  dplyr::select(organ, intervals)

# ---- BEST MODELS ONLY ----
cpg_intervals_Multi_organ_best <- Multi_organ_best_cpg %>%
  group_by(organ) %>%
  summarise(cpgs = list(unique(selected_cpgs)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(intervals = map(cpgs, parse_cpg_intervals)) %>%
  dplyr::select(organ, intervals)

cpg_intervals_overlap_all <- best_cpg_overlap_all_df %>%
   group_by(organ) %>%
  summarise(cpgs = list(unique(selected_cpgs)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(intervals = map(cpgs, parse_cpg_intervals)) %>%
  dplyr::select(organ, intervals)

cpg_intervals_overlap_single <- best_cpg_overlap_single_df %>%
   group_by(organ) %>%
  summarise(cpgs = list(unique(selected_cpgs)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(intervals = map(cpgs, parse_cpg_intervals)) %>%
  dplyr::select(organ, intervals)

###############################################################################
# 6. Core function — interval overlap using foverlaps
###############################################################################

interval_overlap <- function(list_of_dts) {
  
  # Start with the first organ's intervals
  overlap_dt <- copy(list_of_dts[[1]])
  setkey(overlap_dt, chr, start, end)
  
  for (i in 2:length(list_of_dts)) {
    
    dt2 <- copy(list_of_dts[[i]])
    setkey(dt2, chr, start, end)
    
    # Perform interval overlap
    hits <- foverlaps(overlap_dt, dt2, nomatch = 0L)
    
    # CLEAN RESULT:
    # Always reconstruct a fresh interval table with chr/start/end + unique ID
    overlap_dt <- hits[, .(
      chr = chr,
      start = pmax(start, i.start),   # intersected interval start
      end   = pmin(end, i.end),       # intersected interval end
      cpg_id = cpg_id                 # original CpG ID
    )]
    
    # Remove invalid (negative) intervals
    overlap_dt <- overlap_dt[end >= start]
    
    # Stop early if no intervals left
    if (nrow(overlap_dt) == 0L) break
    
    setkey(overlap_dt, chr, start, end)
  }
  
  unique(overlap_dt)
}


###############################################################################
# 7. Wrapper — compute intersections for k-organ combinations
###############################################################################

compute_organ_overlaps <- function(cpg_interval_table, k) {
  
  organ_names <- cpg_interval_table$organ
  combos <- combn(organ_names, k, simplify = FALSE)
  
  map_df(combos, function(combo) {
    
    dt_list <- cpg_interval_table$intervals[cpg_interval_table$organ %in% combo]
    ov      <- interval_overlap(dt_list)
    
    tibble(
      organs = paste(combo, collapse = "_"),
      k = k,
      n_shared = nrow(ov),
      shared_intervals = list(ov)
    )
  })
}

###############################################################################
# 8. Run overlap analyses — all models & best models
###############################################################################

# ---- ALL MODELS ----
overlap_all <- bind_rows(
  compute_organ_overlaps(cpg_intervals_all, 2),
  compute_organ_overlaps(cpg_intervals_all, 3),
  compute_organ_overlaps(cpg_intervals_all, 4)
)



# ---- BEST MODELS ----
overlap_Multi_organ_best  <- bind_rows(
  compute_organ_overlaps(cpg_intervals_Multi_organ_best , 2),
  compute_organ_overlaps(cpg_intervals_Multi_organ_best , 3),
  compute_organ_overlaps(cpg_intervals_Multi_organ_best , 4)
)


###############################################################################
# 9. Output examples
###############################################################################

print(overlap_all)
print(overlap_Multi_organ_best)

# Access example: shared intervals for a all somatic organs x 3 
overlap_all$shared_intervals[7]



```

#### Cpg_number models
```{r 35 }


################################################################################
# 1. Linear mixed model: effect of methodological choices on model performance
################################################################################

# Rationale:
#   - performance_score is continuous → LMM appropriate
#   - organ included as a random effect because each organ contains many 
#     correlated clock models and should not be treated as fixed levels
#   - fixed effects represent methodological decisions that may influence 
#     clock accuracy

metrics_scores <- metrics_data_validation %>%
  group_by(cpg_grouping, model, organ) %>%
  mutate(
    mae_score = scales::rescale(-mae),
    r2_score  = scales::rescale(r_squared_value)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    performance_score = mae_score + r2_score,
    cpg_grouping = factor(cpg_grouping),
    tile_methode = factor(tile_methode),
    model = factor(model),
    organ = factor(organ),
    rsq_threshold = factor(rsq_threshold),
    filter = factor(filter),
    epse_scaled = scale(epse)
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    cpg_data_validation_long %>% 
      dplyr::select(unique_model_id, num_selected_cpg, num_candidate_cpg,selected_cpgs, chr,start,end),
    by = "unique_model_id"
  )

m <- lmer(
  performance_score ~ 
    num_selected_cpg +num_candidate_cpg + (1|selected_cpgs) + (1|chr)+
    (1 | organ),
  data = metrics_scores
)

summary(m)
Anova(m)  # Type-II Wald χ² tests for effect significance

# Interpretation summary (add to manuscript):
#   - tile_methode      : significant moderate effect
#   - model             : strong determinant of performance
#   - rsq_threshold     : significant; correlation filtering matters
#   - filter            : strong effect; CpG coverage thresholds influence accuracy
#   - epse_scaled       : non-significant; training epochs do not influence results
#
# Biological/methodological implication:
#   Structural choices (CpG selection, filtering stringency, model type)
#   drive performance more strongly than hyperparameter tuning.

# Exact CpG optima per organ from your data
cpg_optima <- metrics_scores %>%
  group_by(organ) %>%
  summarise(
    median_cpgs = median(num_selected_cpg),
    iqr_cpgs = paste0("IQR: ", round(quantile(num_selected_cpg, 0.25)), "-", 
                      round(quantile(num_selected_cpg, 0.75))),
    max_perf_cpgs = num_selected_cpg[which.max(performance_score)],
    perf_at_median = median(performance_score[num_selected_cpg <= median(num_selected_cpg)*1.5]),
    max_perf = max(performance_score),
    pct_perf_at_optimal = round((perf_at_median / max_perf) * 100, 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(cpg_optima)
```

## Does the presence of aspecific CpG predict higher model performance

# Give a ranking of CpGs by the average performance of the clocks that contain them.
cpg_effects <- metrics_scores %>%
  group_by(selected_cpgs) %>%
  summarise(
    n_models = n(),
    mean_performance = mean(performance_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_performance = sd(performance_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_performance = median(performance_score, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_performance))
